 NBA Insiders Sound Off on Darius Acuff Jr.'s Playing Style, 'He Needs to Realize It's a Team Game'
 Adam Wells Nov 20, 2026 Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr.'s overwhelming ball-dominance has been the primary talking point around the team so far this season, with people around the NBA wanting to see him evolve his game. 
 Speaking to ESPN's Tim MacMahon , one Eastern Conference scout said "he needs to realize it's a team game" when discussing Acuff and how he needs to grow. 
 "He needs to realize it's a team game," the scout said. "There's no doubt he's a talent. Defensively challenged, to say the least. He can pass — he just doesn't want to pass."

 Bleacher Report 3d On a more positive note, an Eastern Conference executive told MacMahon part of the problem is the situation around Acuff in Sacramento. 
 "He needs to be coached hard and coached well and develop good habits defensively," the executive said. "It's a shame he's going to waste this year with Doug Christie. But he's going to be a stud offensively for sure."
 The Kings made no secret of the fact that Acuff was the player they wanted in the 2026 NBA draft. Things worked out in their favor to take him at No. 7 overall, handing him the keys to the car on offense. 
 Acuff has been more than happy to occupy the driver seat. He is averaging 26.2 points on 22.6 field-goal attempts per game. Luka Dončić (25.6) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (23.3) are the only players taking more shot attempts so far this season. 
 There have been rumblings about potential unhappiness among Kings players, particularly Domantas Sabonis, with Acuff's shot volume. Brendan Nunes of Sactown Sports 1140 poured some cold water on that chatter, noting Acuff and Sabonis have a strong relationship. 
 Even with his high shot volume, Acuff is also racking up assists. He averages 7.0 dimes per game. Dončić and Cade Cunningham are the only other players averaging at least 25 points and seven assists per contest. 
 This isn't to suggest Acuff is anywhere close to that level right now, but the Kings won 22 games last season. They haven't been a good team for a long time, nor are they loaded with talent around Acuff right now that he needs to be deferring to. 
 The key is making sure Acuff doesn't maintain some of his bad tendencies going forward as the Kings try to build their roster around him. 
 Whether that comes from, as the executive said, tougher coaching or just learning from experience, the Kings need Acuff to become a more well-rounded player as they try to build a team that is eventually good enough to compete for a playoff spot in the Western Conference.
